Quotes / Christine de Pizan / Q0541

About Christine de Pizan

Christine de Pizan (1364–c. 1430) was an Italian-born writer active at the French court who authored poetry, political advice books, and The Book of the City of Ladies.

How to read this passage

Across 4 recurring voices here (notably Mary Wollstonecraft and John Locke), equality is framed through Feminist Philosophy and British Empiricism. Some passages define equality; others warn how it fails; still others relocate it inside habit, community, or language. This passage enters that discussion through equality, dignity.

Concepts in this quote

Equality
Equality appears in this archive as a live philosophical concern—not a slogan. These verified English passages show how thinkers treat equality as a problem of judgment, practice, or explanation.
Dignity
Dignity names the worth that persons claim simply as persons—and the respect that worth demands.
